prize_parts.citation: for foundational contributions to the analysis of nominal rigidities and monetary policy: tractable time-dependent price setting, staggered contracts and policy rules, and a microfounded framework for evaluating monetary policy

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B001, with Calvo, Taylor and Woodford. What changed is how I argue it. I no longer rest any part of the case on the framework having 'come through' the post-2021 inflation. The case is that three originating ideas, each tied to specific work, became the benchmark that later theory, estimation and central-bank practice are built on or argued against. Calvo supplied the tractable time-dependent pricing device. Taylor supplied staggered contracts and the policy-rule analysis. Woodford supplied the integrated, welfare-based framework for evaluating policy. The chair asked what separates these three from Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets. My criterion is origin of the idea that later work presupposes. The second group made the framework identified, estimated, canonical and adopted. That is important, but it is a different achievement, and a prize built on it would need a different citation and probably a different laureate set. Under my criterion the trio is the cleanest cut. If the Committee prefers the estimation-and-adoption criterion, I accept that B001 becomes less cleanly bounded than B006. The ideas are 25 to 45 years old, so there is no timing concern. The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises does not cover this core. The case rests on originality, breadth and durability. It does not rest on how many colleagues ranked it highly.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the real cost, and several colleagues have pressed it persuasively. Any three names leave out people with serious claims on the canonical model, identified estimation and adoption. Priority questions involving Fischer and Phelps also remain, and Gertler's place in both B001 and B002 complicates how a macro slot would be allocated. The empirical record is mixed. Micro evidence shows state dependence that the Calvo device does not capture, the Phillips-curve fit is debated, and the 2021-23 episode is unresolved. These points limit what a citation can claim, and I now word it as an analysis and benchmark rather than a validated description. Earlier prizes to Lucas, Kydland-Prescott and Sargent-Sims cover adjacent ground. B006 has a cleaner credit boundary, and the Committee could reasonably weigh that above B001's breadth of influence. I judge it a close call.

responses.point: Strombergmoved from B015 to B001. He qualifies my claim that the framework survived the inflation test, calling the evidence mixed and not a validation. He argues that the award rests on the originating ideas and that the estimation-side claimants extend and quantify rather than originate.
responses.response: I accept the qualification and withdraw any suggestion of validation. The strongest form of the case is that the originating ideas became the standard benchmark, whatever the forecasting record of the estimated descendants. I largely agree with his origin-versus-extension distinction and use it as my criterion. I would add one caution. Christiano, Eichenbaum and their co-authors identified the monetary-policy effects that the framework had to match. A member who values empirical discipline could therefore treat that as part of the discovery, not as mere extension. If the Committee takes that view, the citation and laureate set would change. I would then regard the B001 attribution as less clean than you do.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B006 first and argues that B001's caveats (crowded credit, Gertler's overlap, the post-2008 and post-2021 performance debates) are attribution and durability concerns that B006 mostly avoids. She also challenges 'overdue' as a merit argument.
responses.response: I agree that attribution is B001's main weakness, and she has not overstated it. Where we differ is the weight. I think breadth of demonstrated influence and a clear originating-idea criterion offset it, and B006's weaker cross-country identification and closeness in time to the 2024 prize offset its cleaner credit. I withdraw any reliance on 'overdue'. Elapsed time is a threshold for maturity and is not evidence of merit. Maturity is satisfied in both cases. B006 is my first fallback. If the Committee moves to it, I would support Persson, Tabellini and Besley with her framing: a citation on the formal-plus-empirical framework and its testable predictions, not on settled causal effects of particular constitutions. I would not support a narrowing to two names unless the Committee decides Besley's state-capacity strand is not separable from the joint work.

responses.point: Hassler, the chair, ranks B002 first. He argues that the Kiyotaki-Moore two-author attribution is clean and the mechanism foundational, and that a pair avoids the crowded-credit problem of B001. He accepts that identification of the collateral channel comes mostly from later calibrated and empirical work by others.
responses.response: I agree on the cleanliness of the attribution, and I agree that stylisation is a feature of a foundational mechanism, not a flaw in itself. Two differences remain. First, the 2022 prize covers part of the policy motivation, so I see less unclaimed ground than in B001. Second, the chair's question asks which later empirical work supports the amplification claim. I cannot answer that from the evidence in front of me and will not assert it. Without that evidence I treat the empirical standing as unestablished in this record, which is a weaker basis than B001 has for its direct use in policy analysis. I would regard B002 as a legitimate configuration if the Committee finds the B001 attribution irreducibly messy. I rank B006 and B021 ahead of it, and I do not list it among my two alternatives for that reason.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg says my argument that Calvo, Taylor and Woodford are separable lowered her attribution concern, but she treats the post-2021 Phillips-curve evidence as unresolved. She also says shared first-place rankings should not count as merit.
responses.response: I agree on both points. The Phillips-curve evidence is unresolved, and I should not claim more. The fit problem touches the Calvo device directly, because it is a tractable approximation and not a literal description. I therefore reworded the citation so that it credits 'analysis' and benchmark status and does not imply empirical confirmation. The shared first-place rankings, including those on B001, are not evidence of merit, and I do not use them as such. Your question remains the right one for B002: does the central collateral-feedback claim survive scrutiny? My reservation about it is that I cannot show that it does from this record.

responses.point: Friberg supports the same trio. He points out that his own micro work on menu costs shows mixed time and state dependence, so Calvo pricing is a tractable approximation. He treats this as a limit on the claim and not a refutation.
responses.response: I agree with this limit-not-refutation reading, and I think it answers the chair's question about what the later evidence should do. State-dependent pricing evidence tells us the device is approximate, but that literature still uses the time-dependent and staggered structure as its benchmark. That supports a prize for originating a framework whose assumptions are now tested. It does not support a claim that those assumptions are correct. It does mean the citation must not promise more than that. I take your point that the Taylor rule is the part where scientific contribution and policy practice are hardest to separate, and I would keep the citation to the policy-rule analysis and not to the rule as a prescription.

responses.point: Boppart rejected my round-1 suggestion that quantitative trade models may have superseded part of the heterogeneous-firm framework. He argues that the selection margin survives inside those models and that the remaining issue is credit for Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum.
responses.response: I accept the rebuttal. The Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple margin carries through in the quantitative models, so I withdraw supersession as an objection to B021. The remaining reservation is credit. The empirical regularities and the parallel quantitative route sit outside the entry, so any citation must be centred on the selection model. With that wording I would support Helpman and Melitz as a two-name award, and that is why B021 remains my second alternative. I note that you are a frequent co-author of mine, as disclosed below, and I am not weighing that in the assessment.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee accepts origin of the idea as the criterion for the laureate set, or insists on an estimation-and-adoption criterion that would bring in Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum or Smets and change the citation.

How much the state-dependence evidence, the unresolved Phillips-curve fit and the heterogeneous-agent critique should reduce the weight of a prize centred on the originating ideas, and whether the Taylor rule belongs in the scientific citation.
How the Committee will weigh B001's breadth of influence against B006's cleaner credit boundary and its closeness to the 2024 institutions prize, and whether Besley belongs in a B006 trio.
I rely on general knowledge and the supplied files. I have not independently verified citations, priority claims, adoption figures or the empirical support for the collateral channel.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Calvo, Taylor or Woodford is documented in my supplied profile. I disclose field proximity: my research is in macroeconomic theory, including heterogeneous-agent macro, which is a successor literature to the New Keynesian framework in B001. I have long-standing co-authorships with committee colleagues John Hassler (chair) and Timo Boppart, including the 2018 Myrdal Prize article with Boppart. I am at the Institute for International Economic Studies (IIES). Other members' files refer to Torsten Persson (B006, my alternative) as an IIES colleague. My round-1 note did not repeat this, so I state it now. I have not independently verified the details, and B006 is not my preferred part. My co-authors Golosov, Tsyvinski, Ríos-Rull, Violante and others are not shortlisted candidates, and the profile records none of the B001, B006 or B021 candidates among my co-authors. These are disclosures, not adjudicated, and I assume no recusal.
